scope: Bounded corpus browsing and cold first-command inventory
methodology: Release arm64, private native validation host, production store/actor commands, no real clicks or installed application data.
Each size/variant uses a closed generated seed; each trial copies it. Different variants are equivalent in workload/counts, not byte-identical seeds.
Cold refers to empty application/engine caches; OS disk caches are not purged. Setup, repository construction/index creation, assertions and actual frame painting are outside timers.
First page is data-ready for 100 summaries plus the global count; it is a different milestone from complete store/index readiness.

A summary work count reports returned entry/sense scalar rows, not all SQL rows scanned. Detail work counts report decoded payload rows. Tests separately bound detail SQL work as unrelated corpus size grows.
First favorite uses an archive not warmed by preceding read-only queries. Cold deletion and full-store readiness use separate copies of the same seed.
Visible-entry counters refer to the primary paged browser. Auxiliary deletion/full-load fixture contents and all 1000 retained ratings are checked by separate postconditions.
Prototype variants are intermediate implementations in this change, not a pre-change Dev UI benchmark; cache warming by their old workspace scans affects later windows.
The previous complete 43-window inventory was not rerun. This checkpoint measures eight windows at both sizes, three trials each.
